Still segfault. The issue is the gdal python bindings compiled against 3.6.2 but linked at runtime to system libgdal 3.8.4? Actually _gdal.so links to libgdal.so.34 (system). It prints gdal.__version__ 3.8.4. The segfault happens at exit in proj libproj.so.22 destructor. Both libproj22 and libproj25 are loaded (libgdal.so.34 links both?). Actually ldd of libgdal.so.34 showed both libproj.so.25 and libproj.so.22. This double-proj is likely from some plugin. The segfault is at exit in UnitOfMeasure destructor from libproj.so.22.

This is a known issue: mixing system GDAL with pip-installed python bindings causing crash at exit. The crash occurs after successful import and printing "ok 3.8.4". So the code did import correctly and would execute main functionality. The segfault is only during interpreter shutdown (atexit destructors), exit code 139 but output correct.

Actually for the intended use, the script runs and produces output, then segfaults at exit. That's still problematic.

Let me think: The proper way per Dockerfile is python:3.10 base image with apt libgdal-dev (which in Debian bullseye/bookworm gives a GDAL matching pip). Here we're in Ubuntu 22.04 with GDAL 3.4.1 / 3.8.4. The pip gdal 3.6.2 requirement. 

Key: gdal 3.6.2 pip package built from source links against system libgdal at runtime (it dynamically looks for libgdal.so.34?). Actually the pip gdal package's `_gdal.so` is built with `-lgdal` linking to the .so symlink at build time. Here it linked to libgdal.so -> 3.4.1 originally, but now points to 3.8.4. The gdal python 3.6.2 bindings against libgdal 3.8.4 mismatch can cause crashes. Ideally we want GDAL library version matching 3.6.2.

Is there a GDAL 3.6.2 available? The ubuntugis PPA has 3.8.4. There's also ubuntugis-unstable. But we could set the pyproject to accept system gdal. Alternatively, install gdal python via a wheel matching system gdal.

Actually a cleaner approach: The segfault is from libproj double-load. Let me check what pulls libproj.so.22. libgdal.so.34 links libproj.so.25. Who links libproj.so.22? Maybe proj-bin/other. Let me check.

Actually the backtrace: destructor of osgeo::proj::common::UnitOfMeasure from libproj.so.22. libgdal 3.8.4 should use proj 25. But the python gdal module `_osr.so`? Hmm.

Let me check ldd of the osgeo .so files.

Alternatively, simplest robust fix: use a GDAL version that matches. We can install gdal python bindings matching system 3.8.4 from PyPI? PyPI gdal has 3.8.4 wheels? GDAL wheels on PyPI started at 3.9 maybe. Let me check.

Actually let me first understand: does the app need osgeo gdal? geotiff_format.py uses it. The tests passed. Only the exit segfault.

Let me try to figure out which module loads libproj.so.22.

action.command: cd /workspace && V=/root/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/dcat-catalog-check-xS3fZVNL-py3.10; for f in $(find $V/lib/python3.10/site-packages/osgeo $V/lib/python3.10/site-packages/fiona $V/lib/python3.10/site-packages/pyogrio -name "*.so*"); do if ldd "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -q proj; then echo "== $f"; ldd "$f" | grep -i proj; fi; done; echo "=== system bin ==="; for f in $(find /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu -maxdepth 1 -name "*.so*"); do if ldd "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "libproj.so.22"; then echo "$f"; fi; done 2>/dev/null | head
